title: if, elif & else
intro: Learn the basic ideas of if, elif & else in simple English. Read the explanation and example first; the quiz asks only from the concepts taught here.

items.heading: if statement
items.text: if runs a block when its condition is true. It is used to make decisions.

items.heading: Condition
items.text: A condition is an expression whose result is treated as True or False.

items.heading: elif
items.text: elif means “else if”. It checks another condition when earlier if/elif conditions were false.

items.heading: else
items.text: else provides the alternative block when no previous if or elif condition is true.

items.heading: Comparison in conditions
items.text: Operators such as ==, !=, >, <, >= and <= are commonly used to compare values.

items.heading: Indentation in decisions
items.text: The statements controlled by if, elif and else must be indented consistently.

items.heading: Multiple branches
items.text: One if can be followed by multiple elif branches and an optional else.

items.heading: Truthy and falsy values
items.text: Python treats values such as 0, empty strings and empty collections as false in conditions.

items.heading: Nested conditions
items.text: An if statement can appear inside another block when a decision depends on another decision.

items.heading: Why use conditions?
items.text: Conditions let a program choose different actions based on data instead of always following one fixed path.
